_comment: This file is data, not law. Every entry carries a `source` you can open and
a `confidence` saying how sure the mapping from filename to licence is.
Licences change - Stability relicensed SD3 mid-flight, BFL revised the FLUX
dev terms to v2.0 - so treat `checked` as a best-before date and re-verify
Studios are expected to extend this: add entries to `models` for your own
internally trained weights, or override ours, and pass the file with

apache-2.0.name: Apache License 2.0
apache-2.0.summary: Permissive. Commercial use, modification and redistribution allowed; keep the notice file and state changes.

mit.name: MIT License
mit.summary: Permissive. Commercial use allowed; retain the copyright notice.

bsd-3-clause.name: BSD 3-Clause License
restrictions: No use of the author's name to endorse derived products.
bsd-3-clause.summary: Permissive. Commercial use allowed with attribution and no endorsement claims.

cc-by-4.0.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
restrictions: Credit must be given to the creator.
cc-by-4.0.summary: Commercial use allowed provided you attribute the creator.

cc-by-nc-4.0.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0
restrictions: Non-commercial use only.
Commercial use requires a separate agreement with the rights holder.
cc-by-nc-4.0.summary: Blocks commercial use. Client work, advertising and paid delivery are all commercial.

cc-by-nc-sa-4.0.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0
restrictions: Non-commercial use only.
Derivatives must be shared under the same licence.
cc-by-nc-sa-4.0.summary: Blocks commercial use, and any derivative model must carry the same terms.

creativeml-openrail-m.name: CreativeML Open RAIL-M
restrictions: Use-based restrictions in Attachment A travel with the model and must be passed on to anyone you give it to.
Prohibited uses include generating content that harms minors, disinformation, and unlawful discrimination.
creativeml-openrail-m.summary: Commercial use and commercial output are permitted; the use restrictions must be reproduced downstream.

prohibited_uses: a use-restriction schedule travels with the weights and must be passed on

creativeml-openrail-plus-plus-m.name: CreativeML Open RAIL++-M
restrictions: Use-based restrictions travel with the model and any derivative.
Same prohibited-use list as Open RAIL-M.
creativeml-openrail-plus-plus-m.summary: Commercial use permitted. Outputs are yours; the use restrictions must be passed downstream.

prohibited_uses: a use-restriction schedule travels with the weights and must be passed on

stability-community.name: Stability AI Community License
restrictions: Free for commercial use only while the entity's total annual revenue is under USD $1,000,000.
Above that threshold an Enterprise Licence must be negotiated with Stability AI.
Revenue is measured across the whole entity, not just AI-derived revenue.
Attribution: derivative works must state 'Powered by Stability AI'.
stability-community.summary: Free commercially below USD $1M annual company revenue; a paid enterprise licence above it. The threshold is measured on total company revenue, not AI revenue.

conditions.revenue_basis: total annual entity revenue, not AI-derived revenue

stability-nc-research.name: Stability AI Non-Commercial Research Community License
restrictions: Research and non-commercial use only; commercial use needs a separate Stability licence.
stability-nc-research.summary: Research only. Any paid delivery needs a commercial licence from Stability.

flux1-dev-nc.name: FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License
restrictions: Non-commercial and non-production use only.
Outputs may not be used for any commercial purpose without a licence from Black Forest Labs.
Commercial licences are granted at BFL's sole discretion and may carry a fee, royalty or revenue share.
Commercial deployments are required to report usage through the BFL API.
Content filtering measures are required for all use.
flux1-dev-nc.summary: Non-commercial. Note that the restriction is written to cover the outputs, not only the weights.

tencent-hunyuan-community.name: Tencent Hunyuan Community License
restrictions: Territory is worldwide EXCLUDING the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea - the licence is not granted for use in those jurisdictions.
Products with more than 100 million monthly active users require a separate licence from Tencent.
Derivative works must carry 'Built with Tencent Hunyuan' attribution.
tencent-hunyuan-community.summary: Commercial use allowed outside the EU, UK and South Korea. A UK or EU based facility is outside the granted territory.

conditions.territory_note: the licence grant excludes these territories outright

ltx-community.name: LTX Video Community License
restrictions: Lightricks' community terms gate large-scale commercial use behind a separate agreement; check the revenue and user thresholds for the specific model version.
Attribution to Lightricks is required on derivatives.
ltx-community.summary: Community licence with thresholds rather than a plain open licence - read the version-specific terms before delivery.

insightface-nc.name: InsightFace pretrained model terms (non-commercial)
restrictions: The InsightFace code is MIT, but the pretrained face-analysis models (antelopev2, buffalo_l, buffalo_s) are for non-commercial research only.
Commercial use requires a licence from InsightFace.
Anything trained on InsightFace embeddings inherits the non-commercial restriction.
insightface-nc.summary: Non-commercial, and the restriction is inherited by any face model built on these embeddings - which is why it turns up in face-swap and identity workflows that look permissive from the outside.

s-lab-1.0.name: S-Lab License 1.0 (NTU)
restrictions: Research and non-commercial use only.
Redistribution and use for commercial purposes is not permitted without explicit authorisation.
s-lab-1.0.summary: Non-commercial. Frequently missed because the model ships inside face-restoration node packs.

bria-nc.name: BRIA non-commercial terms (CC BY-NC 4.0 + commercial agreement)
restrictions: Released for non-commercial use; commercial use requires a paid agreement with BRIA.
A self-hosted commercial licence is sold separately.
bria-nc.summary: Background-removal weights released for non-commercial use; commercial use is sold separately by BRIA.

llama-community.name: Llama Community License
restrictions: Products with more than 700 million monthly active users require a separate licence from Meta.
Derivative model names must carry the 'Llama' prefix and display 'Built with Llama'.
Acceptable Use Policy applies.
llama-community.summary: Commercial use allowed for all but the largest platforms, with naming and attribution obligations.

prohibited_uses: an acceptable-use policy is incorporated by reference

qwen-research.name: Qwen research/non-commercial terms
restrictions: Some Qwen variants ship under research-only terms; confirm the exact variant.
qwen-research.summary: Certain Qwen releases are research-only while others are Apache 2.0 - the variant matters.

agpl-3.0-ultralytics.name: AGPL-3.0 (Ultralytics dual licence)
restrictions: AGPL-3.0 requires the complete source of any product that includes the model - your integration code, scripts and configuration - to be released under AGPL-3.0.
Ultralytics state that internal company use inside an automated workflow also requires either an Enterprise Licence or open-sourcing the project.
The network clause means exposing it as a service counts as distribution.
An Enterprise Licence is sold to remove these obligations.
agpl-3.0-ultralytics.summary: Copyleft that can reach the code importing it. Ultralytics sell an Enterprise Licence that removes the obligation.

conditions.copyleft_note: the complete source of anything that includes the model, including integration code, must be released under AGPL-3.0
conditions.vendor_position_internal_use: Ultralytics state that internal production use also requires an Enterprise Licence

proprietary-api.name: Vendor API terms of service
restrictions: Governed by the vendor's terms of service, which can change without notice.
Per-call billing; costs scale with output volume and retries.
Content is transmitted to a third party - check this against client confidentiality and NDA terms.
Output ownership and indemnity vary widely between vendors.
proprietary-api.summary: A hosted model. Commercial rights, cost and confidentiality are set by the vendor contract, not by an open licence.

unknown.name: Unknown
unknown.summary: No licence could be determined. Treat as unclearable until someone confirms the source.

faipl-1.0-sd.name: Fair AI Public License 1.0-SD
restrictions: The licence does not restrict commercial use of the generated images.
It does restrict the model: modifications and derivative models must be released under this same licence, with the changes shared.

A derivative made accessible over a network must offer a way to obtain its source, in the manner of AGPL - so a fine-tune served from a studio's own inference endpoint carries a publication obligation.

Individual models released under FAIPL frequently bolt on their own extra restrictions (commonly a ban on monetised hosted inference), which travel to merges and derivatives. Read the specific model card as well as the licence.
faipl-1.0-sd.summary: Outputs are unrestricted. The model itself is copyleft: derivatives must be published under the same licence, AGPL-style.

playground-v2-community.name: Playground v2 Community License
restrictions: Community licence with use-based conditions; read the model card before commercial delivery.
playground-v2-community.summary: Commercial use permitted under community terms rather than an open licence.

kolors-license.name: Kolors Model License
restrictions: Kwai-Kolors' own model licence; commercial terms and any user thresholds are set there, not by an OSI licence.
kolors-license.summary: Vendor model licence - check the thresholds before commercial delivery.

cogvideox-license.name: CogVideoX License
restrictions: The CogVideoX-2B weights are Apache 2.0; the 5B weights ship under this separate licence. Which variant is loaded decides the answer.
cogvideox-license.summary: Applies to the 5B weights only - the 2B variant is Apache 2.0.

prohibited_uses: an acceptable-use schedule is incorporated by reference

minimax-community.name: MiniMax Community License
restrictions: Territory: the open-weights release excludes local deployment in the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea.
Free commercial use is limited to organisations under roughly USD $20M annual revenue; above that a separate agreement with MiniMax is required.
Commercial products must display 'MiniMax H3' prominently in the user interface.
Outputs may not be used to train competing models, worldwide.
minimax-community.summary: Open weights with a territory carve-out, a revenue cap and a visible-attribution requirement. Where the facility is based matters as much as what it earns.

conditions.territory_note: the open-weights release excludes local deployment in these territories

meta-sam.name: Meta SAM License
restrictions: Research and commercial use are both permitted, including modification and integration.
Prohibited-use terms cover military, ITAR-controlled, nuclear and weapons applications.
More restrictive than a standard permissive licence; read the terms on the weights download page.
meta-sam.summary: Meta's own licence rather than an OSI one. Commercial use is allowed, with a prohibited-use list attached.

notes: Territory exclusions make this one to check against where the facility is based, not just what it earns.
Most Qwen vision-language releases are Apache 2.0, but the family is not uniform - confirm the exact variant.
The wholebody variants are trained on COCO-WholeBody, which carries its own dataset terms.
The only FLUX open-weights model that is commercially clear without a BFL agreement.
Ships under the FLUX.1 [dev] non-commercial terms.
Image editing model under the FLUX.1 [dev] non-commercial licence.
Inpainting variant; same non-commercial terms as FLUX.1 [dev].
The most common licensing trap in modern ComfyUI workflows.
Fine-tunes and LoRAs built on FLUX.1 [dev] inherit the non-commercial restriction.
The FLUX autoencoder is distributed from the FLUX.1 [dev] repository and carries its terms.
The identical file is also mirrored under FLUX.1 [schnell] (Apache 2.0); which terms apply depends on where it was obtained.

provenance_overrides.note: This copy resolves to the FLUX.1 [schnell] repository, which is Apache 2.0, so the dev restriction does not apply to it.

notes: Commercially usable. Predates the Community License, so no revenue threshold applies.
Research-only release; not for commercial delivery.
Commercially usable under Open RAIL-M. Note the ongoing training-data litigation around SD 1.x when assessing indemnity.
Relicensed to the Community License after the original restrictive launch terms.
Free commercially only under $1M annual company revenue; most production facilities exceed that.
Originally research-only, later moved to the Community License - verify which terms your copy shipped under.
The SDXL VAE follows the SDXL base licence when obtained from that repository.
Apache 2.0 - one of the few video models that is commercially clean out of the box.
Google's UMT5 is Apache 2.0; the quantised community repacks used in ComfyUI inherit those terms.
Territory excludes the EU, UK and South Korea - a blocker for facilities based there.
Same territorial exclusions as other Tencent Hunyuan releases.
Community licence with thresholds; confirm the terms for the exact version in use.
CogVideoX-2B is Apache 2.0 but the 5B weights ship under a separate CogVideoX licence.
Check which variant is loaded before assuming commercial rights.
Apache 2.0. Other Qwen model families are not all licensed the same way.
OpenCLIP code and weights are MIT; the LAION training data has its own provenance questions.
The original ControlNet models are Apache 2.0.
Stability's Control-LoRA releases are a separate, more restrictive licence - check which family you have.
IP-Adapter itself is Apache 2.0.
The FaceID variants depend on InsightFace embeddings and are therefore non-commercial in practice.
Explicitly released for non-commercial research use because of its InsightFace dependency.
The repo is labelled Apache 2.0 but requires InsightFace antelopev2, which is non-commercial. The effective licence is non-commercial.
Non-commercial research only. Contact InsightFace for a commercial licence.
InsightFace withdrew public distribution of the inswapper weights; copies in circulation are unlicensed for commercial use.
Also carries obvious likeness and consent exposure in a professional context.
Bundled inside several popular face-restoration node packs, so it often arrives unnoticed.
Apache 2.0, but the architecture borrows from StyleGAN2 whose original NVIDIA source has its own non-commercial terms - worth a legal read for broadcast delivery.
Many of the most popular community upscalers are CC BY-NC-SA, which blocks commercial delivery.
Check the model's OpenModelDB entry - licences differ per author and are frequently unstated.
SAM and SAM 2 model weights are Apache 2.0.
Reaches the ADetailer-style face/hand/person detectors that ship with many custom node packs.
Ultralytics' published position is that internal production use needs an Enterprise Licence.
Common in matting workflows, where the separate commercial agreement is easy to miss.
A commercially clean alternative to RMBG for background removal.
The Base and Large checkpoints are CC BY-NC 4.0; only the Small checkpoint is Apache 2.0.
Depth passes delivered to a client are commercial use.
The Small variant is the commercially usable one in this family.
DWPose is Apache 2.0, but it is distributed alongside YOLOX detectors - confirm the detector's terms too.
Community-trained motion modules vary; only the original Guoyww releases are covered here.
Practical-RIFE has had shifting terms around commercial use; verify before relying on it for delivery.

loras.note: A LoRA's licence is set by whoever trained it and is rarely embedded in the file. It also inherits the obligations of the base model it was trained on - a FLUX.1 [dev] LoRA cannot be more permissive than FLUX.1 [dev].

checkpoints.note: Community merges usually have no stated licence and an untraceable lineage of merged parents. Treat an unmatched checkpoint as unclearable until the source page is checked.

embeddings.note: Textual inversion embeddings inherit the base model's terms and carry the trainer's own conditions.

upscale_models.note: Community upscalers on OpenModelDB are frequently CC BY-NC-SA. Check the author's entry before commercial delivery.
